title: Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Remove as few intervals as possible so that none of the remaining ones overlap.

tests.explain: Keep [1, 3] and [3, 5] (touching at 3 is fine) and remove [2, 4] and [1, 5]. No three of these intervals avoid each other, so 2 removals is the minimum.
All four are the same interval, so only one of them can stay.
The two intervals only touch at 2, which doesn't count as overlapping.

hints: Removing the fewest is the same as keeping the most. How would you choose the largest set of intervals that don't overlap?
Among intervals that clash, keep the one that ends first: it leaves the most room for everything after it.
Sort by end. Walk through, keeping an interval when its start >= the end of the last kept one; otherwise count it as removed.

complexity.time: O(n log n): the sort, then one pass
